answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each voting key to hold its own sealed copy of a public 2 GiB archive of poems and museum notes. Sealing mixes in that key and takes about three hours to redo, so two keys can never share one disk. At random times an auditor asks for one item, such as a sonnet or the entry for a marble bust, and the key must return its sealed hash within one second; a wrong or late reply zeroes its weight. Weight reaches its zenith only after six clean audits. One honest agent keeps one disk; 300 fake keys must keep 600 GiB online. Limit: cheap disks soften it.
